Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and Sri Sanjay Singh, advocate holding brief of Sri Binod Kumar Jha, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the summoning order dated 12.07.2019 as well as entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 2410 of 2018 (Smt. Nisha Khare Vs. Abhishek Srivastava & others), under Sections- 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Nawabad, District- Jhansi pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jhansi.

sentences.text: "Supplementary affidavit alongwith compromise deed has been filed by the learned counsel for the applicants.
The same be kept on record.
Learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and learned counsel for opposite party no.2 are present.
Learned counsel has submitted before the Court that the parties have arrived at a compromise.
The compromise is appended at page-10 of the supplementary affidavit.

It is prayed that as the dispute is matrimonial, the compromise between the parties would not affect the society adversely, but the only section involved is non- compoundable, hence, the trial court be directed to verify the compromise deed of the parties, so that it may be placed before the Court for its acceptance.
The parties are directed to appear before the trial court within 15 days from today alongwith their compromise deed.

If the parties appear before the trial court within the time stipulated, the trial court shall verify the said compromise deed, pass a verification order thereon and transmit the certified copy of the verified compromise deed alongwith the certified copy of the verification order passed thereon, to this Court within 15 days thereafter.

Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant in Complaint Case No.2410 of 2018 (Smt. Nisha Khare v. Abhishek Srivastava & others),
under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. & Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.
Nawabad, District Jhansi, pending before the Chief Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Jhansi."

sentences.text: Pursuant to the order of this Court dated 10.05.2023, learned Additional Civil Judge (Junior Division), Court No. 3, Judicial Magistrate, Jhansi has submitted its report on 23.05.2023 verifying the compromise deed entered into between the parties.

entities.text: Additional Civil Judge (Junior Division), Court No. 3, Judicial Magistrate, Jhansi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sri Sanjay Singh, advocate holding brief of Sri Binod Kumar Jha, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has not objected the aforesaid fact and submitted that opposite party no. 2 does not want to pursue the matter any further.
Therefore, in case proceeding is quashed, he would have no objection.
In view of above, the applicants and opposite party no. 2 do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them.
The matter has been mutually settled between the parties, therefore, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

Thus in view of the well settled principle of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi) Vs. State of Haryana) as well as the judgement of the Apex Court reported in J.T. 2008(() SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Burea of Investigation and another),
Abhishek Srivastava And 3 Ors vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197062145/
2 as well as judgment of the Apex Court reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. Stated of Punjab) and reported in (2014) Supreme Today 642 (Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab and another), the proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
